title: Reliability Coalition: Cross-Team Launch Initiative and Playbook
content:
Summary:
This working plan describes the Reliability Coalition — a temporary cross-functional launch initiative to standardize SLO definitions, measurement, and rollout across Redwood products and deployment modes. The coalition's purpose is to create a repeatable path from SLO definition to production-grade monitoring, alerting, runbooks, and operational handoff. This document is a team-working artifact: rough outlines, owners, dates, and open questions are intentionally included for fast iteration.

Background and motivation:
- Problem: SLOs exist in pockets (hosted API dashboards, dedicated capacity teams, private deployments), but definitions, error budget policies, and rollout processes vary. This makes cross-product incident response inconsistent and increases cognitive load for oncall engineers.
- Opportunity: Create a single lightweight launch pattern (SLO -> dashboard -> alerts -> runbook -> handoff) that teams can adopt in 2–4 sprints. Implement automation templates, a shared observability dashboard, and a governance checklist.

Objectives (SMART):
1) Define canonical SLO templates for the top 3 customer surfaces (hosted API text generation, embeddings, dedicated throughput) by 2026-02-12.
2) Implement measurement pipelines and a shared dashboard that covers 80% of production traffic within 6 weeks of template sign-off (target: 2026-03-26).
3) Pilot rollout with 2 product teams (Console + Dedicated) and complete runbook handoffs and incident play drills by 2026-04-16.
4) Reduce variance in error budget burn reporting across teams to <10% discrepancy by end of pilot.

Scope (in/out):
- In scope: SLO definition template, measurement queries (Prometheus/ClickHouse/BigQuery examples), alert thresholds, runbook templates, canary rollout guide, dashboard panels, training playbook, and automation snippets (Terraform/Helm).
- Out of scope: Long-term SLA legal language, endpoint-level code changes beyond minimal exporter instrumentation, full org-wide enforcement policy (this is a pilot).

Stakeholders and roles:
- Coalition lead: Aisha Patel (eng-sre) — overall coordination, governance decisions.
- Measurement lead: Tom Nguyen (observability) — metrics queries, sampling and cardinality guidance.
- Runbooks & Alerts owner: Lena Martinez (site-reliability) — author runbooks, define oncall actions and playbook steps.
- Product pilot owners: Gillian Park (console) and Mateo Alvarez (dedicated) — product requirements and rollout.
- Platform instrumentation: Rajesh Rao (serving-runtime) — implement exporter hooks and latency histograms.
- Program manager (rotating): assigned per sprint.

High-level timeline and milestones:
Phase 0 — Prep (2026-01-12 to 2026-01-26)
- Kickoff meeting, charter sign-off, stakeholder alignment.
- Inventory current SLOs/dashboards across product teams (owners submit short questionnaire).
Deliverables: Coalition charter, inventory spreadsheet.

Phase 1 — Define (2026-01-27 to 2026-02-12)
- Draft canonical SLO templates (availability, latency, correctness proxies) and error budget policies.
- Produce example measurement queries for p50/p95/p99 latency, availability, and per-route error rates.
Deliverables: SLO template doc, query snippets, acceptance criteria checklist.

Phase 2 — Implement pilot monitoring & dashboards (2026-02-13 to 2026-03-26)
- Instrumentation small experiments: add latency histograms and error counters to runtime for pilot routes.
- Create shared coalition dashboard in Grafana with panels for: SLO status, error budget burn rate, incidents mapped to traces, top N error types.
- Wire alerting rules for burn-rate and immediate-thresholds; define suppression windows for deploy churn.
Deliverables: Grafana dashboard, alert rule set, instrumentation PRs.

Phase 3 — Runbooks, drills & handoff (2026-03-27 to 2026-04-16)
- Author runbooks for top 3 incidents tied to the SLOs (deploy-induced latency spike, backend model OOM, upstream dependency flake).
- Conduct 2 tabletop drills (one daytime, one oncall/night simulate).
- Finalize handoff docs and sign-off criteria for production adoption.
Deliverables: Runbooks, drill notes, handoff signoff.

Phase 4 — Scale & governance (2026-04-17 to 2026-05-30)
- Package templates and automation into a coalition repo with README and adoption checklist.
- Offer 3 office hours sessions for early adopters; gather feedback.
- Prepare lightweight governance cadence: monthly coalition sync for 6 months.
Deliverables: Coalition repo, adoption metrics dashboard, governance calendar.

SLO template (example snippets):
- Surface: Hosted Text Generation API (global)
  - Objective: Availability 99.95% measured over 28-day window (internal signal: route success / total requests excluding client-4xx).
  - Latency objective: p95 response time < 120ms for token-aggregated responses (measured at edge).
  - Error budget: 0.05% over 28d -> burn policy: automated scaling/fallback at 30% burn in a 7d window, paged escalation at 60% burn.
- Surface: Dedicated Inference Pools
  - Objective: Request throughput SLO: 99.9% of 1-minute windows at >= committed throughput.
  - Latency: p95 tail < 200ms for typical seq=512.
  - Error budget and grace period for planned maintenance windows.

Measurement guidance and caveats:
- Use both edge and origin measurements to separate network vs runtime issues. For latency SLOs prefer edge-collected latencies to capture real-customer experience; use origin histograms for root cause.
- Exclude known scheduled maintenance; tag deployments to allow automatic suppression during controlled rollout.
- Be explicit about 4xx treatment: private-deployments may have different client-error semantics, so templates include an optional filter.

Alerts and escalation:
- Two-tier alerting tied to error budget:
  - Burn-level alert (warning): 30% burn in 7d -> slack #sre-reliability-coalition + oncall note. No immediate page.
  - Critical burn (page): 60% burn in 7d or 10% burn in 1d -> page SRE oncall.
- Immediate threshold alerts (page) for sudden outage signals: availability < 99% in 5m or p95 latency > 500ms for 5m.
- All pages must include a runbook link and diagnostic checklist.

Runbook outline (template):
- Incident summary and immediate mitigation steps
- Quick triage checklist (is it region-specific? is it model-serving node OOM? upstream DB?).
- Diagnostic queries and dashboards to check
- Temporary mitigation (rollback, scale up replicas, toggle degraded-mode routes)
- Post-incident tasks and RCA owner assignment

Operational handoff criteria (minimum):
1) SLO template implemented and reporting in coalition dashboard.
2) Runbook published and accessible in drive + linked to PagerDuty escalation.
3) Two successful drills with documented learnings.
4) Product owner sign-off on acceptable burn policy and escalation thresholds.

Metrics of success (how we'll measure progress):
- % of pilot traffic covered by coalition SLOs (goal: 80% by end of Phase 2).
- Number of teams adopting the template within 2 months of pilot (goal: +4 teams).
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for SLO pages during drills vs baseline.
- Variance in error budget reporting across teams (target: <10% discrepancy).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Instrumentation pushes add cardinality/ingestion costs. Mitigation: sampling guidance, aggregated histograms, and budget review with infra finance.
- Risk: Teams resist standardization. Mitigation: lightweight templates, pilot success stories, and office hours.
- Risk: Alert fatigue. Mitigation: conservative defaults, burn-rate tiering, and suppression rules.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- How to treat client-side 4xx errors consistently across hosted vs private deployments? (ACTION: measurement lead to propose filters by 2026-01-20).
- What is the minimal telemetry stomach for private deployments where customers run their own VPC? (ACTION: platform instrumentation to stub a local aggregator pattern).
- Legal/Support: do we expose SLOs publicly as SLAs for Dedicated contracts? (ACTION: connect with legal and sales during Phase 1).

Communication plan and cadence:
- Weekly coalition sync (30m) during Define/Implement phases — rotating minute-taker.
- Dedicated Slack channel for async questions and drill coordination (#sre-reliability-coalition).
- Biweekly office hours during Scale phase.
- Post-mortem and lessons learned doc after each drill; short presentation at Eng All-Hands at end of pilot.

Templates & automation to produce (repo items):
- terraform/grafana-panels/coalition-dashboard.json (exportable panels)
- alerts/prometheus/rules/coalition-rules.yml
- runbooks/coalition-runbook-template.md
- examples/slo-templates/hosted-text-generation.yaml
- ci/instrumentation-checklist.md (pre-merge checklist for runtime changes)

Kickoff agenda (first meeting)
- 0-5m: Welcome, coalition purpose, desired outcomes (Aisha)
- 5-15m: Inventory summary (Tom)
- 15-30m: Draft SLO template review and immediate concerns (Lena + Rajesh)
- 30-40m: Pilot team commitments and milestones (Gillian + Mateo)
- 40-50m: Risks, open questions, next steps, action owners

Appendix: quick cheat-sheet (for engineers)
- Start with the SLO template (file: examples/slo-templates)
- Add latency histograms in runtime for the top 5 routes (recommended buckets included)
- Export success/failure counters with standardized tags (route, region, model-version)
- Add dashboard link to PR and request review from measurement lead

Notes to self (work-in-progress):
- Need to confirm timezones for drills (APAC inclusion).
- Draft of legal note for Dedicated contracts queued with Sales.
- Could we wire a sampled trace link automatically into burn-rate slack messages? Engineering spike needed.

End of document.

(Version history: initial draft 2026-01-12 by Aisha P.; updated 2026-02-15 with measurement snippets by Tom N.; updated 2026-03-05 with drill schedule and pilot commitments.)
